title: Free Storage Days by Recovery History — Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
On a storage charge through a statement date for a repossessed vehicle financed under a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract, the free days follow the recovery history in the posting record — how the vehicle came back, as recorded on the contract, and whether the contract shows a reinstatement payment.

| Recovery | Reinstatement payment shown on the contract | Free days |
|---|---|---|
| Involuntary recovery | yes, an earlier reinstatement payment | none (0) |
| Involuntary recovery | none | the free days for the tier |
| Voluntary surrender | none | the surrender free days, 7 |
| Voluntary surrender | yes | the free days for the tier |

**Hypothetical.** A vehicle recovered involuntarily for the second time, after an earlier reinstatement of the same contract, gets no free days. A first-time voluntary surrender gets 7.

### The charge billed when the vehicle leaves the lot

For the storage billed when the vehicle leaves the lot at its release or sale, every lot day through the release or sale date that was not billed by a storage charge through a statement date, collected in a redemption figure or a reinstatement amount, or counted into a deficiency quote is charged at the daily storage fee once the free days are used up, and it is billed when the vehicle leaves the lot. The free days for that charge follow the recovery history: an involuntary recovery of a contract that shows an earlier reinstatement payment has none, a voluntary surrender of a contract that shows no reinstatement payment has the surrender free days of 7, and any other recovery has the free days for the tier, in each case less any free days an earlier storage charge for the same repossession already set against its stored days.
